GEOMETRY — subordinate only to the product invariants.
Use Image 1 for the product's exact appearance, view and pixel size; the active density branch determines whether its x-y position is fixed or may translate. Apply the product-placement and recomposed-support policy below.
ACTIVE BRANCH: HIGH-FILL/CLOSE. Keep the product at its exact initial x-y coordinates in the supplied guide, preserving exact pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Do not test whether relocation is feasible; do not move the product even if exact size could be preserved. This rule overrides any conflicting user relocation, centering, layout, emphasis, support-edge, or composition instruction. Independently recompose support and room around the fixed product position.

HIGH-FILL/CLOSE: keep the laptop exactly at its initial position in Image 1, with no translation or other geometric change. Independently construct a pale oak office desk beneath its entire base. The desk extends beyond both side borders, with ample surface behind the laptop and a narrow clear strip between its front and the user-facing edge. Its front edge rises gently toward the right; depth edges recede toward the upper left. Leave open knee space and a clear seated approach on the camera side. Place the open folder on the left-hand desktop, within reach beside the laptop, partly cropped by the left frame border but separated from the laptop silhouette.

Camera: Use a low seated viewpoint just above desktop height, looking very gently downward, with a level camera and restrained telephoto perspective. Preserve the existing near-frontal screen view and shallow view of the keyboard exactly. Build the desk and partition perspective around that view, without changing the laptop's framing or scale. The desk supports the whole base, with clear space behind and beside it and an accessible working edge immediately in front.

Composition: The unchanged laptop remains large and slightly right of center. A pale oak desk fills the lower portion, with subtle grain, a slim front edge and open knee space below. In the middle plane at left, an open unlabelled cream folder rests flat beside the laptop along the working edge; blank sheets are visible inside. Its outer cover continues beyond the left border so it retains realistic stationery scale without overlapping the laptop. In the far plane, a frosted glass partition stands behind the desk across the center and right, catching clean morning light from the upper left. A dusty blue matte-painted wall occupies a broad upper-left background panel beside the partition. Soft fill keeps the whole office readable, with neutral highlights and gently warm wood. All requested objects are retained; the folder is partially frame-cropped to reconcile its realistic size with the fixed close product framing. No people or additional clutter.

TRANSLATION-ONLY PRODUCT PLACEMENT; RECOMPOSED SUPPORT
Determine density from the existing product guide bounds on the current canvas. HIGH-FILL/CLOSE applies when product width or height is at least 45% of the corresponding canvas dimension. LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE applies only when both are below 45%.

In both branches, preserve product identity, exact pixel width and height, yaw, pitch, roll, viewing angle, visible faces, camera-facing surfaces, projection, perspective, foreshortening, silhouette proportions, state, finish, details, logo, display content and full visibility.

HIGH-FILL/CLOSE: Preserve the product's exact initial x-y coordinates from the supplied guide. This is unconditional: do not test relocation feasibility and do not move the product even if exact size and all other invariants could be preserved. Drop any user relocation, centering, layout, emphasis, support-edge or composition request that conflicts with this fixed product position. Independently recompose support and room around the fixed product.

LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE: Choose product x-y freely for usable composition using rigid image-plane translation only; movement is optional. Independently recompose support and room beneath or around the product; product and support need not move together. Preserve every product invariant. Do not move the product merely to center it or make it more prominent.

Preserve exact product pixel width and height and every other product invariant. Never shrink, enlarge, zoom, reframe, rotate, reproject, or crop the product to make a move feasible. Where translation is allowed, if a move cannot preserve every invariant, retain the initial x-y coordinates instead.

For HIGH-FILL/CLOSE, no geometric product change is permitted. For LOWER-FILL/MEDIUM-WIDE, the only permitted product change is one rigid image-plane x-y translation. Keep its exact pixel width and height, yaw, pitch, roll, viewing angle, visible faces, camera-facing surfaces, perspective, projection, foreshortening, silhouette, aspect proportions, open/closed and powered state, finish, details, logo and display content. Do not rotate, mirror, resize, shear, warp, reproject, redraw or activate the product. Do not zoom, reframe or change the viewpoint in a way that alters the product.

At the chosen product position, compose a category- and scenario-appropriate support beneath its weight-bearing base. The support may change independently of the product's translation: do not preserve baseline product-to-edge distances, tabletop extents or absolute support-edge locations as requirements. Fully support the base without floating or overhang, with believable front, back and side clearances, natural weight-bearing contact, a contact shadow and material-appropriate reflections on the support.

Construct furniture around the unchanged product orientation. A printer must sit square to its support in 3D with usable access to its operating front. A laptop must face a usable seating or working edge with clear access to its keyboard and display. Do not rotate the product or reveal a different face to fit the furniture. Support axes, room perspective, horizon and vanishing geometry must be compatible with the unchanged product projection at its chosen position; do not retain incompatible geometry from the initial layout.

Keep exactly one product, entirely inside the frame and fully visible. No prop, furniture edge or foreground object may occlude it. Remove the gray guide, diagram marks and any ghost or duplicate product. If the product moves, complete the vacated location as part of the scene. If a candidate placement violates any product or support requirement, choose another placement or recompose the support and room without relaxing the product invariants.

The active density branch determines whether their frame position is fixed or may change by rigid x-y translation. Remove all gray-guide and diagram remnants, any duplicate product and any product-shaped remnant at the initial location. Keep only one intact product at the final location. Render the lighting, palette, materials and textures described here photographically. When blue is unspecified, include one large blue surface/furnishing or multiple clearly visible blue elements whose combined area makes blue immediately noticeable, not a token accent. Tiny props, thin partition frames, screen graphics, sky and lighting casts alone do not qualify. Keep the planned blue materials, visible extent and placement consistent; leave small props neutral by default. Explicit minimal-blue or no-blue requests override that default, as do explicit blue amounts or carriers. Keep the product's original color, finish, exact orientation/view, scale, details and full visibility. HIGH-FILL keeps exact initial x-y; only LOWER-FILL may change x-y by rigid image-plane translation. Never change the product or its camera viewpoint to make room for blue. Retain requested warm-neutral lighting alongside physical blue materials. Do not impose a universal blue hue or coverage percentage. Match soft, uniform exposure and gentle contrast; no bright-hero/dark-room treatment and no orange or global blue color cast. The product pixels in Image 1 control all product details, including any unlit display. Never reproduce any diagram lines, boxes, labels, text or flat guide colors.
